forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Salford repaid a £21m LOBO loan after lender proposed 7.76%, and expects £48m more to be called
news_drafts.lead:
Salford City Council repaid a £21m LOBO loan in September 2026 after the lender proposed raising its interest rate from 4.75% to 7.76%. A LOBO is a bank loan where, on set dates, the lender may propose a higher rate and the council may then repay the loan in full instead of accepting it. The council's mid-year treasury management report to the Overview and Scrutiny Board says the loan, which had a final maturity of 1 September 2066, was repaid without penalty from cash balances.

The report also records £30m of new three-year borrowing "to refinance" the £21m loan. Its Table 14 lists two £15m loans from other local authorities at 4.90%, maturing in August 2029. The paper does not explain the £9m difference between the £21m repaid and the £30m borrowed.

The council has £62m of LOBO loans with call dates up to 31 March 2027. Following advice from its treasury advisers, Arlingclose, it says: "Based on this assessment, it is considered likely that £48m of these loans will be called." It plans to repay any called loan at no additional cost rather than accept the revised terms. Its LOBO balance fell from £163m on 1 April 2026 to £142m at 30 September 2026.
news_drafts.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB

news_drafts.headline: Salford housing service forecasts £3.6m overspend and cannot meet £1m savings target after mid-year transfer
news_drafts.lead: Salford's housing service, transferred to the Place Directorate mid-year, is forecasting a £3.6m overspend driven by housing benefit subsidy losses and demand pressures in supported housing and housing options. The service cannot deliver its budgeted £1m savings target. In a statement to the scrutiny panel, the council said the service is "not yet sufficiently embedded within the directorate to identify, develop and deliver sustainable savings of this scale without risking service performance" and will need to develop a fresh plan once new leadership arrangements are in place. After drawing £1.76m from reserves, the net overspend stands at £1.8m. The housing capital programme has also been reproffiled down by £17m as contract arrangements are finalised, with the council acknowledging risks to future delivery from staffing and third-party dependencies.
news_drafts.paper_title: Report - Q1 - Place Directorate budget report - LMB HAP

news_drafts.headline: Salford misses accounts deadline for second year as auditors plan third disclaimer of opinion
news_drafts.lead: Salford City Council has failed to publish its draft accounts for 2025/26, missing the 30 June statutory deadline by nearly three months. The council faced the same delay last year, when accounts were published on 25 September due to problems valuing its property, plant and equipment (long-lived assets such as buildings). Auditors plan to issue a disclaimer of opinion for the third consecutive year, meaning they will not have completed enough work to confirm the accounts are correct. The council's auditors have identified a new risk of significant weakness in how it manages statutory financial reporting. The council is transitioning to a new financial system during 2026/27, and auditors have engaged specialists to verify that data transfers correctly before the next audit begins.
news_drafts.paper_title: Salford City Council Audit Progress Report Sept 2026

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB
findings.headline: Section 13.1 says no short-term borrowing has been taken this year, while Table 3 records £30.000m of short-term borrowing
findings.detail: Section 3.4 describes the £30m of new borrowing as long-term, with a three-year maturity. Table 3 and Table 14 show it as short-term borrowing from local authorities. Section 13.1 then says no short-term borrowing has been taken this financial year. The paper does not reconcile these descriptions.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council reviewing the same report would need to know how the £30m is classified, since it affects the maturity profile and the liquidity figures that lenders rely on.
findings.figures: £30m new borrowing; Table 3 short-term borrowing £30.000m at 4.900%; local authority loans of £15.0m and £15.0m at 4.90% maturing 20/08/29 and 07/08/29
findings.quote: The council has also not taken any short-term borrowing so far in this financial year

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB
findings.headline: The liability benchmark rises from £261.5m in 2027 to £426.2m in 2029, against existing borrowing of £285.8m
findings.detail: The paper says the current capital programme and the schemes reprofiled to 2027/28 and 2028/29 mean additional borrowing will be needed in future years. Internal borrowing is forecast to rise from £256.6m to £293.4m, and funds available for investment to fall from £72.7m to £40.0m.
findings.matters: A council moving from a long-term investor position to a borrower will need new loans, and lenders and peers can see the scale of the expected gap against current borrowing.
findings.figures: Liability benchmark £261.5m in 2027, £371.4m in 2028, £426.2m in 2029; existing borrowing £285.8m; internal borrowing £256.6m actual and £293.4m forecast for 2027; available for investment £72.7m and £40.0m
findings.quote: Based upon the current capital programme for 2026/27 and the schemes reprofiled to 27/28 and 28/29 there would need to be additional borrowing in future years.

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB
findings.headline: Capital spend was £36.0m at 30 September against a revised 2026/27 estimate of £124.4m, up from an original £111.2m
findings.detail: The paper says the main decrease in forecast spend is due to schemes being reprofiled into future years. The revised estimate is, however, higher than the original, and the borrowing requirement falls from £75.1m to £56.8m while grants rise from £36.8m to £67.6m. Appendix 2 forecasts capital expenditure of £138.2m in 2027/28.
findings.matters: A large gap between spend to date and the revised full-year estimate, with the change funded more by grants than borrowing, is a delivery and funding question for any council planning similar schemes.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure original estimate £111.2m; spend to 30 September £36.0m; revised estimate £124.4m; grants original £36.8m and revised £67.6m; borrowing requirement original £75.1m and revised £56.8m; 2027/28 estimate £138.2m

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB
findings.headline: Salford proposes applying £5.218m of its £14.940m HRA reserve, built from tower block defect compensation, to historic Pendleton Tower sprinkler and legal costs
findings.detail: A review concluded that expenditure from 2017/18 to 2025/26 on sprinkler works and legal and inspection fees relates to HRA assets. It was originally funded from unsupported borrowing and General Fund resources. The paper proposes that the HRA reserve pay for it, and states that the change creates no additional borrowing requirement or call on council reserves.
findings.matters: Moving historic General Fund and borrowing-funded costs onto a ring-fenced HRA reserve is an unusual correction, and other councils with HRA defect compensation may face the same question about where the costs belong.
findings.figures: £5.218m historic expenditure applied from HRA reserve; sprinkler works £3.624m; capital legal and inspection fees £0.911m; historic revenue legal fees £0.598m; current year legal fees £0.085m; compensation received £14.940m
findings.quote: It is proposed that £5.218m of this reserve is utilised to finance the identified historic expenditure

findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Midyear update Report for 2026-27 v4 OSB
findings.headline: The PWLB certainty rate for 10-year loans was 5.62% at the start of the period and 6.17% at the end
findings.detail: The paper gives PWLB 20-year rates of 6.13% to 6.61% and 50-year rates of 6.01% to 6.37% over the same period. Gilt yields rose over the half-year, with the 10-year gilt yield moving from 4.86% to 5.43%. The council has said it will repay LOBOs where possible and replace them, usually from the PWLB or other local authorities.
findings.matters: Replacement funding for any called LOBO is priced off these rates, so a finance director comparing a 4.75% LOBO with a 6.17% PWLB 10-year rate can see the cost of replacement that the council faces.
findings.figures: PWLB 10-year certainty rate 5.62% at start of period and 6.17% at end; 20-year 6.13% to 6.61%; 50-year 6.01% to 6.37%; 10-year gilt 4.86% to 5.43%
findings.quote: The PWLB certainty rate for 10-year maturity loans was 5.62% at the beginning of the period and 6.17% at the end.
